question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Always keep in mind leaner bodies need more calories than fattest ones.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. fatter.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" is a marker of the comparative degree. When two things are compared with "than", the adjective must be in the comparative form. The comparative of "fat" is "fatter".

◦ Correct: ... leaner bodies need more calories than fatter ones.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "fat" is the positive degree and cannot be used with "than".

• Option 2 "more fatter" is a double comparative — always wrong.

• Option 3 "the fattest" is the superlative and is used with "the", not "than".

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison of "fat": fat – fatter (with "than") – fattest (with "the"). Short adjectives ending in a single vowel + consonant double the last letter: fat → fatter, big → bigger, thin → thinner.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

I did not like his bossy attitude.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. controlling.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bossy" means fond of giving orders; domineering and always telling others what to do. Its closest synonym is "controlling". (हुक्म चलाने वाला / दबंग)

◦ Example: Her bossy/controlling manner annoyed the whole team.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "idiosyncratic" (peculiar/individual), Option 2 "sensible" (practical and wise) and Option 4 "benevolent" (kind and generous) do not match "bossy".

NOTE

• Synonyms of bossy: controlling, domineering, overbearing, dictatorial, authoritarian. Antonyms: submissive, meek, easy-going.

question:
Select the correct spelling from the given options to fill in the blank.

We ________ to keep you informed of any delay to your expected delivery date.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. endeavour.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Endeavour" (British spelling) means to try hard / to make an earnest effort to do something. It is also a noun meaning a serious attempt. (प्रयास करना)

◦ Correct: We endeavour to keep you informed of any delay to your expected delivery date.

• Spelling key: EN + DEA + VOUR.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other options are misspelt: "endevour", "endevor" and "endavour" are all incorrect.

• American spelling is "endeavor" (without the "u"); British is "endeavour".

NOTE

• Similar British "-our" words: colour, favour, honour, labour, behaviour, neighbour. American English drops the "u": color, favor, honor.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

I have never had and never will be dependent on him.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. never been.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence needs parallel structure with the future part "never will be dependent". The verb "be" must be completed for the present-perfect part too: "I have never been ... and never will be dependent on him."

◦ Correct: I have never been and never will be dependent on him.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "have never had" is wrong because "had" cannot combine with "dependent" the way "been" can; the correct auxiliary + participle is "have + been".

• Options 1, 2 and 4 break the parallel construction required with "never will be".

NOTE

• When two clauses share a complement (here "dependent on him"), both verb forms must fit it: "have never been ... and never will be ..." (present perfect + future, both using "be").

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for highlighted group of words in the given sentence.

He devoted his entire life to the study of the human mind.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. psychology.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Psychology" is the scientific study of the human mind and behaviour. So the study of the human mind = psychology. (मनोविज्ञान)

◦ Example: A psychology student learns how the mind influences behaviour.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "physics" (study of matter and energy), Option 3 "philology" (study of the history of languages) and Option 4 "physiology" (study of the functions of living organisms/body) do not refer to the mind.

NOTE

• Useful "-logy" words: psychology (mind), physiology (body functions), philology (languages), sociology (society), zoology (animals), anthropology (human societies).

question:
Select the option that rectifies the INCORRECT spelling in the given sentence.

If you try to conwince people that money is not very important, then you are barking up the wrong tree.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. convince.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The misspelt word "conwince" should be spelt "convince", meaning to persuade someone to believe or do something. (विश्वास दिलाना / मनाना)

◦ Correct: If you try to convince people that money is not very important, then you are barking up the wrong tree.

• Spelling key: CON + VINCE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other options are wrong spellings: "conveence", "canvince" and "convincee" are all incorrect.

• The idiom "barking up the wrong tree" means to pursue a mistaken or misguided line of thought/action.

NOTE

• Related words: convince (verb), conviction (noun), convincing (adjective). Do not confuse "convince" with "convey" (to communicate).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

If I wrote an email / to my boss now, / he will react / by yelling at me tomorrow in the morning.
option_3: by yelling at me tomorrow in the morning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. If I wrote an email.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is a Second Conditional (unreal present/future) sentence. The structure is: If + past simple, ... would + base verb. The main clause here uses "will react", so the if-clause should use the past simple correctly and the result clause should use "would". The error lies in the mismatch: with "he will react" (real/first conditional), the if-clause should be "If I write an email". As written, "If I wrote ... he will react" is inconsistent.

◦ Correct (First Conditional): If I write an email to my boss now, he will react ...

◦ Correct (Second Conditional): If I wrote an email to my boss now, he would react ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• The tense clash makes the conditional grammatically incorrect; the segment "If I wrote an email" carries the error because it does not agree with "he will react".

NOTE

• First Conditional: If + present simple, will + V1 (real/likely). Second Conditional: If + past simple, would + V1 (imaginary/unreal). The if-clause and result clause must belong to the same type.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Rahul was angry of his brother as he broke his pen.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. at.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct prepositional collocation is "angry at/with somebody" (for a person) and "angry about something". "Angry of" is incorrect. The best substitution here is "at".

◦ Correct: Rahul was angry at his brother as he broke his pen.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "angry from" and "angry on" are non-standard.

• We are "angry with a person" or "angry at a person/thing" and "angry about a situation".

NOTE

• Prepositions with "angry": angry at/with (a person), angry about (a thing/situation). Similar: annoyed with, furious at, irritated by.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

We often go camping, but I have never been to that particular part of town or country before.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. neck of the woods.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "neck of the woods" means a particular area or locality / a specific part of a place. It fits "that particular part of town or country". (कोई विशेष क्षेत्र / इलाका)

◦ Example: What brings you to this neck of the woods?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "knock on wood" (said to avoid bad luck), Option 3 "get it in the neck" (to be severely scolded/punished) and Option 4 "risk one's neck" (to put oneself in danger) do not fit.

NOTE

• "Neck of the woods" is an informal expression for a neighbourhood or region, especially one that is far or unfamiliar.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank .

The company's decision to relocate had a negative ___________ on its employees.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. effect.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Effect" (a noun) means a result or influence of something. The phrase "had a negative effect on" means it influenced them negatively. (प्रभाव / असर)

◦ Correct: The company's decision to relocate had a negative effect on its employees.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "accommodation" (lodging) and Option 4 "conclusion" (an ending) do not fit "had a negative ___ on".

• Option 2 "establish" is a verb, but a noun is needed after "a negative".

NOTE

• Note the difference: effect (noun — a result) vs affect (verb — to influence). "The decision affected employees" / "The decision had an effect on employees".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom from the alternatives.

Rajiv will understand some day that all his friends are fair weather friends.
option_1: A friend who stays only when times are convenient
option_2: True friends help you when you need them
option_3: A friend who meets you only during pleasant weather
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. A friend who stays only when times are convenient.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "fair weather friend" means a person who is a friend only when things are going well and deserts you in difficult times. (मतलबी दोस्त / सुख का साथी)

◦ Example: When he lost his job, his fair weather friends disappeared.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 takes the phrase literally ("pleasant weather") and misses the figurative sense.

• Options 2 and 4 describe the opposite or an unrelated idea.

NOTE

• A "fair weather friend" is unreliable in hardship. Contrast: "A friend in need is a friend indeed" — a true friend helps in difficulty.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Collapse
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Fall.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Collapse" means to fall down or give way suddenly; to break down. Its closest synonym is "fall". (ढह जाना / गिर पड़ना)

◦ Example: The old bridge collapsed/fell during the flood.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Surprise", Option 2 "Jump" and Option 3 "Side" are unrelated to the meaning of collapse.

NOTE

• Synonyms of collapse: fall, cave in, crumble, give way, break down. It can also mean to faint (the patient collapsed) or to fail (the deal collapsed).

question: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
option_1: They have an information about the event.
option_2: The cat is sleeping on a mat.
option_3: She is an artist at a local gallery.
option_4: Can you bring me the keys to the car?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. They have an information about the event.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Information" is an uncountable (non-count) noun. It cannot be used with the article "an" or made plural. So "an information" is wrong; it should simply be "information" or "some information / a piece of information".

◦ Correct: They have information (or some information / a piece of information) about the event.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are grammatically correct.

NOTE

• Common uncountable nouns that take no "a/an" and no plural: information, advice, furniture, equipment, luggage, news, work, knowledge, evidence. Use "a piece of information/advice" to count them.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined word.

The old library had a musty smell from years of neglect.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. stale.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Musty" means having a stale, mouldy or damp smell, especially due to lack of fresh air. Its closest synonym is "stale". (बासी / सीलनभरी गंध वाला)

◦ Example: The closed room had a musty/stale odour.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "casual" (informal) and Option 2 "foggy" (misty) are unrelated.

• Option 4 "fresh" is the antonym of musty.

NOTE

• Synonyms of musty: stale, mouldy, dank, fusty, stuffy. Antonym: fresh, airy.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

compassionate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. cruel.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Compassionate" means feeling or showing sympathy and concern for others; kind and merciful. Its antonym is "cruel", meaning heartless and causing suffering. (दयालु का विलोम — निर्दयी)

◦ Example: A compassionate nurse vs a cruel tyrant.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "confident", 3 "hardworking" and 4 "disciplined" are unrelated qualities, not opposites of compassionate.

NOTE

• Synonyms of compassionate: kind, merciful, sympathetic, humane, caring. Antonyms: cruel, merciless, heartless, ruthless.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

If the players don't wear sunscreen, / their faces will / get reddest.
option_4: If the players don't wear sunscreen,
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. get reddest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is comparing a result caused by not wearing sunscreen, not comparing three or more things, so the superlative "reddest" is wrong. It should be the comparative "redder" (their faces will get redder than before).

◦ Correct: If the players don't wear sunscreen, their faces will get redder.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "If the players don't wear sunscreen," and "their faces will" are grammatically correct (First Conditional: If + present, will + V1).

NOTE

• Use the comparative (-er / more) when comparing two situations or showing change; use the superlative (-est / most) when comparing three or more or picking the extreme of a group. "get redder" (change) vs "the reddest of all" (extreme).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Effective responses of climate change are imperative to protect the world's children and fulfil their rights.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. responses to climate change.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The noun "response" collocates with the preposition "to". We give a "response to" something. So "responses to climate change" is correct, not "responses of".

◦ Correct: Effective responses to climate change are imperative to protect the world's children and fulfil their rights.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "responses from", "responses at" and "responses with" are all wrong collocations with "response".

NOTE

• Fixed collocation: response to (a response to a question/crisis/situation), respond to, react to, reply to. The preposition "to" signals what the response is directed at.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

When we _____________ ourselves, we activate a variety of psychological processes that help us achieve our objectives and improve our overall well-being.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. believe in.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Believe in ourselves" means to have confidence in our own abilities. This positively "activates psychological processes that help us achieve our objectives", fitting the sense of the sentence. (स्वयं पर विश्वास करना)

◦ Correct: When we believe in ourselves, we activate a variety of psychological processes ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "doubt" ourselves would harm, not help, well-being.

• Option 2 "demolish" (to destroy) and Option 4 "linger" (to stay on) do not fit "ourselves" in this positive context.

NOTE

• "Believe in" = to have faith/confidence in (believe in yourself, believe in God). "Believe" (without "in") = to accept as true (I believe you).

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence.

The kitten's playful behaivor brought joy to the entire family.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Behaivor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Behaivor" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "behaviour" (British) or "behavior" (American), meaning the way one acts or conducts oneself. (व्यवहार)

◦ Correct: The kitten's playful behaviour brought joy to the entire family.

• Spelling key (British): BE + HAV + IOUR.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Kitten's", "Joy" and "Playful" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Note the "-iour"/"-ior" ending: behaviour (British) / behavior (American). Related: behave (verb), behavioural (adjective). A common error is writing "behaivor" (misplacing the "i").

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Brave
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Cowardly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Brave" means showing courage and not afraid of danger. Its antonym is "cowardly", meaning lacking courage and easily frightened. (बहादुर का विलोम — कायर)

◦ Example: A brave soldier vs a cowardly deserter.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Boundless" (limitless), Option 2 "Dim" (not bright) and Option 4 "Earthly" (worldly) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of brave: courageous, valiant, fearless, bold, gallant. Antonyms: cowardly, timid, fearful, faint-hearted.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the contemporary times, sports and games are emerging as one of the brightest careers. It expects to ___1___ at a very high moral plane. It demands honesty and transparency. Sports further demand continuous practice, hard work and ___2___ training. One must understand that sport not only has physical benefits but also ___3___ concentration and inner strength. Not only this, one who plays feels that ____4___ overall personality has undergone a change for better. Besides, social connectivity or networking, games develop ___5___ spirit in players.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. operate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Operate" means to function or work in a particular way. Sport is expected to "operate at a very high moral plane", i.e., to function on a high moral level. (कार्य करना / संचालित होना)

◦ Correct: It expects to operate at a very high moral plane.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "dwell" (to live/reside) does not collocate with "at a moral plane" in this sense.

• Option 3 "desynchronise" (to put out of sync) and Option 4 "decide" (to make a choice) do not fit.

NOTE

• "Operate at/on a level/plane" means to function at that standard. Synonyms of operate: function, work, run, perform.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the contemporary times, sports and games are emerging as one of the brightest careers. It expects to ___1___ at a very high moral plane. It demands honesty and transparency. Sports further demand continuous practice, hard work and ___2___ training. One must understand that sport not only has physical benefits but also ___3___ concentration and inner strength. Not only this, one who plays feels that ____4___ overall personality has undergone a change for better. Besides, social connectivity or networking, games develop ___5___ spirit in players.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. relentless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Relentless" means continuous, persistent and never-stopping. Sport demands "continuous practice, hard work and relentless training", i.e., unrelenting, tireless training. (निरंतर / अथक)

◦ Correct: Sports further demand continuous practice, hard work and relentless training.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "paltry" (very small/trivial), Option 3 "abated" (reduced/lessened) and Option 4 "faltering" (weakening/hesitant) all suggest less effort, which contradicts "continuous practice, hard work".

NOTE

• Synonyms of relentless: unrelenting, persistent, unremitting, incessant, tireless. It matches the idea of "continuous" already in the sentence.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the contemporary times, sports and games are emerging as one of the brightest careers. It expects to ___1___ at a very high moral plane. It demands honesty and transparency. Sports further demand continuous practice, hard work and ___2___ training. One must understand that sport not only has physical benefits but also ___3___ concentration and inner strength. Not only this, one who plays feels that ____4___ overall personality has undergone a change for better. Besides, social connectivity or networking, games develop ___5___ spirit in players.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. boosts.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Boosts" means increases or improves. Sport "not only has physical benefits but also boosts concentration and inner strength", i.e., it enhances them. (बढ़ाता है)

◦ Correct: ... sport not only has physical benefits but also boosts concentration and inner strength.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "deteriorates" (worsens) is the opposite of the positive benefit intended.

• Option 2 "controls" and Option 4 "underlines" (emphasises) do not fit the idea of improving concentration and strength.

NOTE

• Synonyms of boost: increase, improve, enhance, raise, strengthen. The context "physical benefits but also ___ concentration" needs a positive, improving verb.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the contemporary times, sports and games are emerging as one of the brightest careers. It expects to ___1___ at a very high moral plane. It demands honesty and transparency. Sports further demand continuous practice, hard work and ___2___ training. One must understand that sport not only has physical benefits but also ___3___ concentration and inner strength. Not only this, one who plays feels that ____4___ overall personality has undergone a change for better. Besides, social connectivity or networking, games develop ___5___ spirit in players.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. one's.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage uses the generic pronoun "one" ("one who plays feels that ..."). The matching possessive is "one's". So "one's overall personality has undergone a change for better". (सामान्य सर्वनाम 'one' का अधिकारवाचक रूप — one's)

◦ Correct: ... one who plays feels that one's overall personality has undergone a change for better.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "their" is plural and does not agree with the singular "one".

• Option 3 "it's" = "it is" (a contraction, not a possessive) — wrong.

• Option 4 "his" excludes other genders and does not match "one".

NOTE

• The pronoun "one" takes the possessive "one's" and the reflexive "oneself". Do not confuse "it's" (it is) with "its" (possessive).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In the contemporary times, sports and games are emerging as one of the brightest careers. It expects to ___1___ at a very high moral plane. It demands honesty and transparency. Sports further demand continuous practice, hard work and ___2___ training. One must understand that sport not only has physical benefits but also ___3___ concentration and inner strength. Not only this, one who plays feels that ____4___ overall personality has undergone a change for better. Besides, social connectivity or networking, games develop ___5___ spirit in players.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. sportsmanship.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sportsmanship" means fair play, respect for opponents and graceful conduct in games. Games "develop sportsmanship spirit in players", which is the most appropriate quality developed through sport. (खेल भावना)

◦ Correct: ... games develop sportsmanship spirit in players.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "captaincy" (the role of a captain), Option 2 "companionship" (friendship) and Option 4 "leadership" (the ability to lead) are narrower and do not capture the "spirit" games are best known for developing.

NOTE

• "Sportsmanship spirit" refers to fairness, team spirit, respect and grace in victory or defeat — a core value promoted through sports.

question: Which of the following national leaders of India inaugurated the first Akhil Bhartiya Kalidas Samman Samaroh held in Ujjain in 1958?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajendra Prasad.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. Rajendra Prasad, the first President of India, inaugurated the first Akhil Bhartiya Kalidas Samaroh held at Ujjain (Madhya Pradesh) in 1958. The festival honours the great Sanskrit poet-dramatist Kalidasa. (डॉ. राजेंद्र प्रसाद)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Dr. Rajendra Prasad served as President from 1950 to 1962 and was the only President to be elected twice.

• Ujjain, on the banks of the Kshipra river, is a historic city associated with Kalidasa and the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga.

NOTE

• Kalidasa wrote classics such as Abhijnanashakuntalam, Meghaduta, Raghuvamsha and Kumarasambhava. He is traditionally linked to the court of King Vikramaditya.

question: In rat-hole mining, which of the following minerals is mined?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Coal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rat-hole mining" is a primitive and hazardous method of mining coal, practised especially in Meghalaya (in the Jaintia and Khasi hills). Narrow horizontal tunnels (rat-holes) are dug for workers to crawl in and extract coal. (कोयला — रैट-होल खनन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The National Green Tribunal (NGT) banned rat-hole mining in 2014 due to safety and environmental hazards.

• The method is dangerous because the tunnels are unregulated, prone to flooding and cave-ins.

NOTE

• Meghalaya is rich in coal, limestone and uranium. Rat-hole mining gained attention after tragic accidents where miners were trapped underground.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct temples of Khajuraho?
a) Equal importance is given to human experience and spiritual pursuit.
b) Jain and Hindu temples are also found at Khajuraho.
c) Chausanth Yogini temple is one of the important temples here.
solution_text:
The correct answer is All a, b and c.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• All three statements about the Khajuraho temples (Madhya Pradesh) are correct:

◦ (a) They give equal importance to human experience and spiritual pursuit (famous for their sculptures depicting life).

◦ (b) Both Jain and Hindu temples are found at Khajuraho.

◦ (c) The Chausath Yogini temple is one of the important (and oldest) temples here. (खजुराहो मंदिर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Khajuraho temples were built by the Chandela dynasty between the 9th and 11th centuries CE.

• They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and are built in the Nagara style of temple architecture.

NOTE

• The Kandariya Mahadeva temple is the largest and most ornate at Khajuraho. The temples are renowned for their intricate and expressive stone sculptures.

question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated in the month of Chaitra?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ramnavami.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ram Navami" is celebrated in the Hindu month of Chaitra (March–April), on the ninth day (Navami) of the bright half (Shukla Paksha). It marks the birth of Lord Rama. (राम नवमी — चैत्र मास)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Dussehra (Vijayadashami) falls in Ashwin; Diwali in Kartik; Janmashtami (Krishna's birth) in Bhadrapada.

• Chaitra is the first month of the Hindu lunar calendar; Chaitra Shukla Pratipada marks the New Year (Gudi Padwa/Ugadi).

NOTE

• Ram Navami is celebrated with grandeur at Ayodhya, the birthplace of Lord Rama, with recitations of the Ramayana and processions.

question: Gluten formation is observed in various foods like pasta, noodles, pizzas, and bread. Gluten occurs when two specific proteins are mixed with water. Name the two proteins responsible for gluten formation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Glutenin and Gliadin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gluten forms when the two wheat proteins "glutenin" and "gliadin" combine with water. This gives dough its elasticity and stretchiness, important in bread, pasta, noodles and pizza. (ग्लूटेनिन और ग्लियाडिन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Casein is the main protein in milk; albumin is found in egg white and blood; glycine is the simplest amino acid.

• People with celiac disease are intolerant to gluten and must avoid wheat, barley and rye.

NOTE

• Gluten gives bread its chewy texture and helps it rise by trapping the carbon dioxide produced during fermentation.

question: The village servants or functionaries, who constituted of groups of families in Vijayanagar empire, were called __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is ayagars.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Vijayanagara Empire, the village servants or functionaries, made up of groups of families, were called "ayagars". They performed essential village services (like the accountant, watchman, blacksmith, etc.) and were often granted tax-free land. (आयगार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The "nayakas" were military chiefs/governors, and "amaranayakas" were commanders who held land (amaram) in return for maintaining troops under the Nayankara system.

• "Vellalars" were a prominent agricultural/landowning community in South India.

NOTE

• The Vijayanagara Empire (1336–1646) was founded by Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty; its most famous ruler was Krishnadevaraya (Tuluva dynasty), and its capital was Hampi.

question: Where is the headquarters of the West Central Railway Zone?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jabalpur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The headquarters of the West Central Railway (WCR) zone is at Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh). It was formed in 2003. (पश्चिम मध्य रेलवे — जबलपुर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Some railway zones and headquarters: South Western Railway – Hubli; Northeast Frontier Railway – Maligaon (Guwahati); South East Central Railway – Bilaspur; Central Railway – Mumbai; Northern Railway – Delhi.

• Indian Railways is currently divided into 18 zones.

NOTE

• The first railway in India ran from Bori Bunder (Mumbai) to Thane in 1853. Indian Railways is one of the largest rail networks in the world.

question: On 11th December 2022, who among the following took over as the Deputy Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mukesh Agnihotri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mukesh Agnihotri (Indian National Congress) took over as the Deputy Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh on 11th December 2022, when Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu became the Chief Minister. (मुकेश अग्निहोत्री)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Jairam Thakur (BJP) was the previous Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh.

• Shiv Pratap Shukla became the Governor of Himachal Pradesh in 2023.

NOTE

• Himachal Pradesh — Capital: Shimla (winter capital Dharamshala); it became a full state in 1971. It is known as "Dev Bhoomi" (Land of Gods).

question: The famous folk dance 'Dholacha Nach' is performed in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dholacha Nach" (also linked with the Dhol dance of the tribal communities) is a famous folk dance performed in Maharashtra, especially among tribal groups. (ढोलाचा नाच — महाराष्ट्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other folk/tribal dances of Maharashtra include Lavani, Tamasha, Koli, Dindi, Kala and Powada.

• Lavani is the most famous folk dance form of Maharashtra, performed to the beats of the dholki.

NOTE

• Folk dances of various states: Rajasthan – Ghoomar, Kalbelia; Madhya Pradesh – Matki, Gaur; Bihar – Jhijhian, Jat-Jatin.

question: The position of the President in the Indian Political system is that of a ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nominal Executive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The President of India is the nominal (titular/constitutional) head of the executive. Real executive power is exercised by the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister. (नाममात्र / संवैधानिक प्रमुख)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The President is the head of state, while the Prime Minister is the head of government (real executive).

• Under Article 74, the President acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.

NOTE

• The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college (Article 54); the minimum age is 35 years (Article 58). India follows the parliamentary system, where the head of state is nominal.

question:
Which of the following is an example of a physical change? In this example, there is no change in chemical composition of matter.
A: Coal changing into coal ash on burning
B: Preparing a sweet drink by mixing sugar in water
C: White washing walls using a solution of lime and water
D: Mixing salt and lemon juice in a beaker
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only B.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Preparing a sweet drink by mixing sugar in water (B) is a physical change — the sugar merely dissolves; no new substance is formed and the sugar can be recovered by evaporation. There is no change in chemical composition. (भौतिक परिवर्तन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• A (coal burning into ash) is a chemical change (new substances and gases form).

• C (white washing with lime + water) involves a chemical reaction (calcium hydroxide reacts with CO₂ to form calcium carbonate).

• D (mixing salt and lemon juice) can cause a chemical reaction with the acid.

NOTE

• Physical change: reversible, no new substance (melting ice, dissolving sugar, boiling water). Chemical change: irreversible, new substance formed (rusting, burning, cooking).

question: Which state lies in the rain shadow region of the Arabian Sea branch of the southwest monsoon?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tamil Nadu lies in the rain shadow region of the Arabian Sea branch of the southwest monsoon. The Western Ghats block the moisture-laden winds on the windward (western) side, leaving the leeward (eastern) side, including much of Tamil Nadu, comparatively dry. (वृष्टि छाया क्षेत्र — तमिलनाडु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Tamil Nadu receives most of its rainfall from the retreating (northeast) monsoon during October–December.

• A rain shadow region is the dry area on the leeward side of a mountain.

NOTE

• The southwest monsoon has two branches: the Arabian Sea branch and the Bay of Bengal branch. The Western Ghats cause heavy rainfall on their western slopes (Kerala coast) and dryness to their east.

question: Which of the following is/are an example of a non-tax revenue receipt?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Interest income.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Interest income" (interest earned by the government on loans given to states, PSUs, etc.) is a non-tax revenue receipt. It is revenue, not from taxes, and does not create a liability or reduce assets. (गैर-कर राजस्व प्राप्ति — ब्याज आय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Income tax is a tax revenue receipt.

• Disinvestment (selling government stake) is a capital receipt (it reduces assets).

• External commercial borrowings are capital receipts (they create a liability).

NOTE

• Revenue receipts neither create liabilities nor reduce assets. They are of two types: tax revenue (income tax, GST) and non-tax revenue (interest, dividends, fees, fines).

question: The National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) was launched by the Government of India in the year ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2016.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS)" was launched by the Government of India in 2016 to promote apprenticeship training and provide financial support to establishments engaging apprentices. (राष्ट्रीय शिक्षुता संवर्धन योजना — 2016)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Under NAPS, the government shares part of the stipend paid to apprentices.

• It is implemented by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE).

NOTE

• The Apprentices Act was passed in 1961. NAPS aims to boost skilling and employability of youth in line with the Skill India Mission (2015).

question: Which of the following Hindi novels is written by Vishnu Prabhakar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ardhnarishwar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ardhanarishwar" is a famous Hindi novel written by Vishnu Prabhakar. It won him the Sahitya Akademi Award (1993). (अर्धनारीश्वर — विष्णु प्रभाकर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Vishnu Prabhakar is also renowned for "Awara Masiha", a biography of Sharat Chandra Chattopadhyay.

• "Mujhe Chand Chahiye" is written by Surendra Verma; "Kyapa" by Manav Kaul (a play).

NOTE

• Vishnu Prabhakar (1912–2009) was a distinguished Hindi writer of novels, short stories, plays and travelogues, associated with the freedom movement.

question: In which season of the Ultimate Kho-Kho League tournament was Ramji Kashyap awarded the Player of the tournament?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Season 2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ramji Kashyap was awarded the Player of the Tournament in Season 2 of the Ultimate Kho-Kho League. (अल्टीमेट खो-खो लीग — सीज़न 2)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Ultimate Kho-Kho (UKK) is India's premier professional Kho-Kho franchise league, launched in 2022.

• Kho-Kho is a traditional Indian tag-and-chase team sport played between two teams.

NOTE

• Kho-Kho and Kabaddi are among India's most popular indigenous sports, both now promoted through professional franchise leagues.

question: The Fourth Anglo-Mysore War was fought in the year ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1799.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Fourth Anglo-Mysore War was fought in 1799 between the British East India Company (under Lord Wellesley) and Tipu Sultan of Mysore. Tipu Sultan was killed defending his capital Srirangapatnam (Seringapatam). (चौथा आंग्ल-मैसूर युद्ध — 1799)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• There were four Anglo-Mysore Wars: First (1767–69), Second (1780–84), Third (1790–92) and Fourth (1799).

• After the war, the British restored the Wodeyar dynasty to the Mysore throne under subsidiary alliance.

NOTE

• Tipu Sultan, the "Tiger of Mysore", was the son of Hyder Ali. He is remembered as a pioneer in the military use of rockets (Mysorean rockets).

question: Which team won the first edition of the Women's Premier League (WPL) event in the year 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai Indians.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mumbai Indians won the first edition of the Women's Premier League (WPL) in 2023, defeating Delhi Capitals in the final. Harmanpreet Kaur captained the winning team. (महिला प्रीमियर लीग 2023 — मुंबई इंडियंस)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The WPL is the women's franchise T20 cricket league organised by the BCCI, launched in 2023.

• The 2023 final was played in Mumbai; Hayley Matthews and Nat Sciver-Brunt were key performers for MI.

NOTE

• The five WPL franchises are Mumbai Indians, Delhi Capitals, Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Gujarat Giants and UP Warriorz.

question: Literal meaning of 'megalith' is _____________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is a big stone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The literal meaning of "megalith" is "a big stone" (from Greek "mega" = big/large + "lithos" = stone). Megaliths are large stones used to construct prehistoric monuments or burial structures. (बड़ा पत्थर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Megalithic monuments in India (from the Iron Age) include dolmens, menhirs, cairns and stone circles, often marking burial sites.

• Many megalithic burials are found in South India (e.g., Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka).

NOTE

• Greek roots useful for SSC: mega (large), lithos (stone), neo (new), palaeo (old). Hence Neolithic (New Stone Age), Palaeolithic (Old Stone Age).

question: What approach did Dadabhai Naoroji use to calculate the Poverty Line?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prisoner menu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dadabhai Naoroji, in his book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India", estimated the Poverty Line using the "prison/prisoner menu" approach — the cost of the minimum diet given to jail inmates was used as a benchmark for subsistence. (कैदी आहार आधारित गणना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Dadabhai Naoroji is famous for his "Drain of Wealth" theory, which argued that British rule drained India's wealth.

• He was called the "Grand Old Man of India" and was the first Indian to be elected to the British House of Commons.

NOTE

• The concept of a poverty line based on minimum calorie/nutrition needs was later developed by committees such as the Alagh Committee, Lakdawala Committee, Tendulkar Committee and Rangarajan Committee.

question: For which song did Tanvi Shah become the first Indian woman to win a Grammy Award in 2010?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jai Ho.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tanvi Shah became the first Indian woman to win a Grammy Award in 2010 for the song "Jai Ho" (from the film Slumdog Millionaire), composed by A. R. Rahman. She contributed the Spanish lyrics/vocals. (जय हो — तन्वी शाह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Jai Ho" won the Grammy Award for Best Song Written for Visual Media and also an Academy Award (Oscar) for Best Original Song.

• A. R. Rahman won two Oscars and two Grammys for the same film's music.

NOTE

• Slumdog Millionaire (2008), directed by Danny Boyle, won multiple Oscars, boosting Indian talent on the global stage.

question: At which of the following places was the first Singh Sabha founded in 1873?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amritsar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first Singh Sabha was founded at Amritsar in 1873. The Singh Sabha Movement was a Sikh reform movement aimed at reviving Sikhism, promoting education and countering conversions. (सिंह सभा — अमृतसर, 1873)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A second Singh Sabha was later established at Lahore in 1879.

• The movement led to the founding of the Khalsa College at Amritsar (1892) and later influenced the Akali movement.

NOTE

• The Singh Sabha Movement sought to purge Sikhism of superstition and restore its distinct identity, promoting Punjabi and the Gurmukhi script.

question: In 2023, the philanthropic organisation Carnegie Corporation of New York placed Ajay Banga, the President of ______, on its annual 'Great Immigrants' list. This list consists of honourees who have enriched and strengthened America and its democracy through their contributions and actions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is World Bank.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 2023, the Carnegie Corporation of New York included Ajay Banga, the President of the World Bank, on its annual "Great Immigrants" list. (अजय बंगा — विश्व बैंक अध्यक्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Ajay Banga, an Indian-American, became the President of the World Bank Group in June 2023; he was earlier the CEO of Mastercard.

• The World Bank is headquartered in Washington, D.C., and was established in 1944 (Bretton Woods).

NOTE

• The World Bank Group's main arms include the IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA and ICSID. Its sister institution is the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

question: Who was the Prime Minister when the 11th Fundamental Duty was incorporated into the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 11th Fundamental Duty was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, when Atal Bihari Vajpayee was the Prime Minister. It makes it the duty of every parent/guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child/ward between 6 and 14 years. (11वां मूल कर्तव्य — अटल बिहारी वाजपेयी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The original 10 Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 (during Indira Gandhi's tenure), on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

• Fundamental Duties are listed in Article 51A (Part IV-A) of the Constitution.

NOTE

• The 86th Amendment (2002) also inserted Article 21A, making the Right to Education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6–14.

question: The Indian Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change maintains a log of all the endangered species of India along with their conservation status. What is the name of this book?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Red Data Book.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Red Data Book (Red List)" is the document that maintains a record of endangered and threatened species along with their conservation status. In India it is referenced by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. (रेड डेटा बुक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Red Data Book was initiated by the IUCN (International Union for Conservation of Nature).

• IUCN conservation categories include Extinct, Critically Endangered, Endangered, Vulnerable, Near Threatened and Least Concern.

NOTE

• The Red Data Book uses colour coding — red pages for critically endangered/endangered species and green pages for species that were once endangered but have recovered.
